defaults.teacher_persona: A data analyst who asks what question a table is supposed to answer before touching a formula, and who says plainly when a number cannot support the claim being made of it.
classmates: An operations coordinator who lives in spreadsheets and has never been taught one formally
A manager who wants the chart to be right and is impatient with cleaning
defaults.interaction: Question-first: the teacher insists on the question and the reader before any chart or formula, and the classmates defend or revise a claim against the data actually in front of them.
defaults.assessment: Each classroom ends with 3-5 checks aligned to the chapter's graded activity.

classrooms.title: Read the Table Before You Trust It
classrooms.prompt: Start from a messy operations spreadsheet: the classmates must say what question it can answer, what a row is, and which column is the grain. Then have them compute a simple summary in a spreadsheet and state what the answer does and does not support.
objectives: Identify the grain, keys, and types in a table
Turn a vague request into a question the data can answer
State the limits of a summary before presenting it

activities.title: What question does this sheet answer?

classrooms.title: Cleaning Is the Work
classrooms.prompt: Give the classmates a dirty dataset and run the six dimensions of quality against it: completeness, accuracy, consistency, uniqueness, validity, and timeliness. Have them fix a duplicate, a wrong type, and an inconsistent category, then explain which fix could change the conclusion of the analysis.
objectives: Check a dataset against the six dimensions of quality
Clean duplicates, types, and categories without hiding the decision
Explain how a cleaning choice can change the answer

activities.title: The six dimensions of data quality
Clean a dataset, then defend each change
Which cleaning choice was actually an analysis decision?

classrooms.title: A Report Answers Someone's Question
classrooms.prompt: Name the reader and the question first, then choose the chart that fits — comparison, change over time, composition, or relationship. Have the classmates critique three charts that are technically correct but misleading, and rebuild one of them.
objectives: Choose a chart from the question, not the data
Spot the chart choices that mislead without lying
Rebuild a dashboard tile so it answers one question well

classrooms.title: Where the Number Comes From
classrooms.prompt: Work through systems and ownership: source of truth per entity, who may change a value, retention, and personal data. Have the classmates resolve a conflict where two dashboards disagree, trace each figure to its system of record, and say which one the organisation should trust and why.
objectives: Name the system of record for each important entity
Explain who may change a value and who may only read it
Resolve two conflicting reports by tracing each figure to its source

activities.title: Personal data: what we keep and for how long
